title: Autopilot Reserve Hypotheses - 1:1 Prep & Follow-ups
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with Alex (capacity lead) about prototyping an "autopilot reserve" flow that reduces committed spend while protecting steady-state throughput for customers with predictable diurnal patterns.
- Want a set of testable hypotheses, one-week experiment plan, and clear follow-ups.

Top-level hypotheses (ranked):
1) Micro-reservations reduce committed GPU delta by ~15–25% for mid-size customers without impacting 95th pct latency.
   - Why: commit only for high-confidence windows (cron-like or usage-signal), autoscale fills short gaps.
   - Risk: mispredicted windows cause spillover into burst pool -> potential throttling.
2) Overbooking (statistical multiplexing) across customer pools can increase utilization by ~7–12% if we keep per-customer SLO buffers.
   - Why: customers rarely peak simultaneously across regions.
   - Risk: correlated peaks (product launches) will violate SLO unless fallback path is robust.
3) Price-tiered burst (cheap spot-like burst credits) reduces visible customer cost for infrequent peaks while preserving committed base.
   - Why: customers accept lower guarantees for cheaper burst credits.
   - Risk: complexity in billing and explaining guarantees.

Experiment plan (one-week quick run):
- Scope: 3 mid-size customers (non-prod + prod-like traffic), one dedicated pool of 32x GPU baseline.
- Setup: implement autopilot-controller that watches 30d history, generates next-week micro-reserve suggestions (2-6h blocks), then applies to a test-subpool (8 GPUs) with canary traffic.
- Metrics to collect: committed-GPU-hours, pool-utilization, 95/99 latency, request rejection rate, cost delta per-customer.
- Success criteria: commit-hours drop >=10% with <1% increase in 95th latency and 0.1% increase in rejections.
- Rollback: auto-revert micro-reserves if 95th latency increases >2x baseline over 15m window.

Quick back-of-envelope numbers (rough):
- Baseline pool: 32x A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Typical steady commit: 24 GPUs. Peak bursts consume 30–32 for ~3h/day on average.
- Target: shave 3–5 committed GPUs via micro-reserve -> 12–20% reduction.
- Cost assumptions (rough): $X per GPU-hour (use infra sheet later) -> savings approx (3 GPUs * 24h * 30d) = 2160 GPU-hours/month avoided if fully effective (best case).

Questions to ask Alex in 1:1:
- Operational: how comfortable is SRE with automated placement/unplacement of reserved instances? Any hard limits from our infra allocator?
- SLA & legal: do we need new contract clauses for micro-reserve windows or is it within existing dedicated terms? (cc: legal?)
- Billing: can current invoicing represent partial reserved-hours buckets (e.g., 4h blocks) without large bookkeeping work?
- Capacity: which pools are safe to run experiments in (canary pool ids)?
- Signal: which telemetry do we prioritize for prediction (last-7d diurnal, traffic spike detectors, customer-provided schedule)?

Potential implementation approaches (fast -> more effort):
- Heuristic windows (fast): simple pattern mining for daily/weekly peaks; propose fixed blocks. Low lift, brittle.
- ML predictor (medium): simple time-series model (seasonal ARIMA/Prophet) per-customer to forecast busy windows. Needs training but better generalization.
- Reinforcement/autotune (high): controller that learns cost-latency tradeoff via bandits. More infra & safety work.

Edge cases / gotchas to note:
- Multi-region customers: need to tie reservations to region-level pools; cannot shift globally without draining KV cache — heavy perf impact.
- Hot reloads: removing a reserved GPU quickly can evict cached KV and increase latency for long-context models. Add cooldowns.
- Model heterogeneity: some models are much more latency sensitive to GPU churn; mark those as "no-autopilot".
- Customer communication: need opt-in, show projected savings and impact surface.

Immediate action items to list at the end of the 1:1:
- Alex: confirm safe canary pool ids and SRE owners (due 2026-02-24).
- Me (Priya): prototype heuristic micro-reserver script + dashboard ingest by 2026-02-28.
- Ethan: add billing representation spike to billing team + sample invoice line item by 2026-03-05.
- Clara: draft customer opt-in email template and FAQ by 2026-03-03.

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Keep experiment simple: only one knob (reserve/unreserve). No pricing changes in week-1.
- Collect logs at 1s granularity for first 48h after any reserve change to detect KV thrash.
- Put guardrails around any automation: human-in-the-loop approval toggle for first 2 weeks.

Slack links / tickets I need to add to doc after 1:1:
- /msg alex about canary pool ids
- Create JIRA ticket for micro-reserve-run-epic (link into linked_artifacts)

Open questions for follow-up thread:
- How do we define "steady-state" for billing reconciliation? 7d median? 30d trimmed mean?
- Do we allow overlapping micro-reserves across customers on same pool or treat them as additive?

Final quick script idea (pseudo):
- input: historical 30d per-hour usage for customer X
- detect: windows where usage >= 80% of peak for 60+ contiguous minutes at least 3 times/week
- propose: 2–6h reserve blocks covering 80% of those windows
- apply: write reservation to test API or flag for manual approval

End of notes — keep this as my 1:1 agency doc. Will copy selected bits into a more formal spec if Alex signs off.
